cards.summary: I grew up in Goa, got hooked on PC games at seven, and started writing little games at eight.
cards.heading: Then, making them
cards.body: I got hooked on PC games when I was seven. By eight, I was writing little games of my own.

cards.summary: Computer science in 11th and 12th grade, with C/C++ as my main languages, pointed me toward computer engineering. Being house captain got me into leadership, public speaking, and debate.
cards.heading: C, C++, and an audience
cards.body:
I had computer science as a subject in 11th and 12th grade. I was good at it, and computer engineering felt like the obvious next step.

Being house captain introduced me to leadership, public speaking, and debate, irrespective of how many people wanted to hear my opinions.

cards.summary: Dengue put me in hospital before finals. I still finished Class 12 in the national top 0.01% for CS and went to GEC, Goa University, for computer engineering.
cards.heading: Dengue, right before finals
cards.body:
A few weeks before my Class 12 final exams, complicated dengue put me in hospital for a month.

I still finished Class 12 in the national top 0.01% for CS and started my BE in Computer Engineering at Goa Engineering College, Goa University.

Mosquitoes and I have not reconciled.

cards.summary: At GEC I learned to live on my own, found Python through PyCon, won seven hackathons, placed nationally in IEEE Xtreme's top ten, and finished among the top students with a 3.7 GPA.
cards.heading: The syllabus had competition
cards.body:
College was my first time living on my own. I had a lot to figure out.

I discovered Python at PyCon.

Hackathons became minibosses: seven wins in four years, plus a national top-ten finish in the 24-hour IEEE Xtreme.

I finished among the top students in my class with a 3.7 GPA. This was becoming a bit of a trend.

chapters.heading: Six months. A lot of Java.

cards.summary: I moved to Pune for HSDI, finished first in six months of Java training, and went on to lead five developers building banking utilities.
cards.heading: A proper training program
cards.body:
I joined HSDI (HSBC Software Development India) in Pune. First came six months of Java training. I finished, you guessed it, at the top of the class.

C/C++, Python, now Java. Gotta catch 'em all. I went on to lead five developers building banking utilities.

chapters.heading: Surely a script can do this.

cards.summary: Banking red tape pushed me toward automating manual work and building TasKing in Java/Swing. Wanting more to learn, I looked at US universities and did well on GRE and TOEFL.
cards.heading: Bored, not done
cards.body:
Banking red tape blocked new work, so I started automating the manual stuff and building apps like TasKing, which I wrote in Java/Swing.

I wanted to learn more, so I looked at US universities, then took the GRE and TOEFL. I did really well. Again.

cards.summary: At SJSU, I was Prof. Paul's only student to score the maximum 110% and became his TA. I automated grading, built student leaderboards, and made the Alexa-powered campus chatbot SpartanBot.
cards.heading: Prof. Paul, 110%, and competitive homework
cards.body:
SJSU was affordable and gave me the challenge I wanted. In Professor Paul Nguyen's class, I scored 110%, the maximum possible, and was his only student to do it.

I was promptly made his TA. I built a Docker/Python autograder and live student leaderboards.

I also built SpartanBot, an Alexa-powered campus chatbot.

chapters.period_label: Jun-Aug 2018 / Google Hardware/Nest, during my MS
chapters.heading: Good news, everyone!

cards.summary: My Google Hardware/Nest internship, during the MS, showed me how much I enjoyed developer tools, direct feedback, and choosing the right language for the job. Imposter syndrome came with plenty to learn.
cards.heading: Google, during my master's
cards.body:
Google Hardware/Nest felt different. Everyone wanted to build cooler products, and the culture was playful.

I could pick whatever language suited the problem. I built tools and infrastructure for developers and got feedback directly from them. This was the work I wanted.

I had imposter syndrome around engineers far better than me. Learning from them was intimidating, intoxicating, addictive. I left wanting more.

cards.summary: I joined Salesforce in 2019 and moved to San Francisco. I cut Chat release prep from months to minutes and helped move its monolith to AWS, with room to explore beyond an internship's fixed end date.
cards.heading: And room to explore
cards.body:
I joined Salesforce in 2019 and moved to San Francisco.

I automated Chat release prep, cutting months of manual work down to minutes. I also helped move the monolith from data centers to AWS.

Full-time work didn't have my internship's fixed end date. I had room to explore, surrounded by smart people.

cards.summary: During COVID, I had to find a pace I could sustain without burning myself out.
cards.heading: A pace I could keep up
cards.body: During COVID, I had to find a pace I could keep up without burning myself out.

cards.summary: Bots reached 99.99% availability after CI/CD and monitoring work. I worked on its API, contributed to the Slack connector, migrated all customer traffic from Heroku to multisubstrate public cloud, and moved to Copilot's configurable agents.
cards.heading: Reliability, APIs, then LLMs
cards.body:
On Einstein Bots, I improved CI/CD and monitoring, including Argo CD, and got the service to 99.99% availability. I also worked on its public API and seamlessly migrated 100% of customer traffic from Heroku to multisubstrate public-cloud instances.

My contribution to the public Slack connector was a small part of that API work.

When LLMs arrived, I moved to Einstein Copilot: a platform for talking to a configurable AI agent inside Salesforce.

cards.summary: As a Principal engineer on Agentforce, I help customers build agents through Atlas, AgentScript, voice, memory, MCP, async work, and long-running sessions. I also build team DevOps tools. My enthusiasm, drive, and passion are at an all-time high.
cards.heading: Principal, not finished
cards.body:
Then came Agentforce: a platform where Salesforce customers could build their own agents. Basic topics and actions grew into the Atlas Reasoning Engine and AgentScript, making agent behavior more deterministic in an LLM world.

We're adding voice, MCP, native context, memory, an agentic runtime, async processing, and long-running turns, actions, and sessions.

I enjoy connecting Salesforce CRM data to the agent platform. I'm learning and growing. I also build context-aware DevOps tools for my team: a work assistant and coding harness. My enthusiasm, drive, and passion are at an all-time high.

discoveries.heading: More from GEC
discoveries.body:
I became my department's general secretary.

During my Zuari internship, I saw enterprise software running in an on-premise SAP data center for the first time. I built a PHP dashboard and monitoring tools with Python alerts.

I presented a paper on securing voice and video calls.
discoveries.summary: Department general secretary, a first look at enterprise SAP during my Zuari internship, and a paper on securing voice and video calls.

discoveries.heading: Games and custom ROMs
discoveries.body:
I made 3D Tic-Tac-Toe and, at GEC, a C++ Snake graphics project.

From 18 to 20, I worked on CyanogenMod for the Samsung Galaxy Ace in Southeast Asia.
discoveries.summary: I made 3D Tic-Tac-Toe and C++ Snake, and worked on CyanogenMod for the Galaxy Ace from 18 to 20.

discoveries.heading: Green Belt and CI/CD
discoveries.body:
My Lean Six Sigma Green Belt project saved over 2,000 hours of manual work.

Separate CI/CD work cut time to market by 25%.
discoveries.summary: My Green Belt project saved 2,000+ hours of manual work. Separate CI/CD improvements cut time to market by 25%.

discoveries.heading: The Coldplay cameo
discoveries.body: That's my silhouette at 3:41 in Coldplay's "In My Place" video for Oxfam. It also became my Gmail picture.
discoveries.summary: My silhouette appears at 3:41 in the Coldplay/Oxfam video for "In My Place." It became my Gmail picture too.

discoveries.heading: Opportunity Hack
discoveries.body: At PayPal's Opportunity Hack, I worked on an Alexa project for the City of San Jose. We placed second.
discoveries.summary: I placed second at PayPal's Opportunity Hack with an Alexa project for the City of San Jose.

discoveries.heading: The rest of my MS
discoveries.body:
My MS in Software Engineering focused on enterprise systems and cloud computing. I finished with a 3.90 GPA.

I also worked as a research assistant using JavaScript and Python.
discoveries.summary: An MS in Software Engineering with a 3.90 GPA, focused on enterprise systems and cloud computing, plus research work in JavaScript and Python.

discoveries.heading: Tools I built at Google
discoveries.body:
I built a Python/Dremel dashboard to track a Nest web app's performance.

I also built tooling to create Jira issues when tests failed.
discoveries.summary: A Python/Dremel performance dashboard for a Nest web app and tooling to create Jira issues from failed tests.

discoveries.heading: Senior, Lead, Principal
discoveries.body: I became Senior in October 2020, Lead in August 2023, and Principal in February 2025.
discoveries.summary: Senior in October 2020, Lead in August 2023, and Principal in February 2025.

discoveries.heading: Corporate awards are meaningless
discoveries.body:
I still kept the list: TMP All Star (top 1% of Salesforce contributors), Rising Star, SPOT, PEARL, Above and Beyond, and an AppSprint win.

I was HSDI's youngest Rising Star nominee at 20. HSDI is HSBC Software Development India.
discoveries.summary: HSDI's youngest Rising Star nominee at 20, plus TMP All Star, Rising Star, SPOT, PEARL, Above and Beyond, and AppSprint recognition. I still kept the list.

discoveries.heading: Still playing
discoveries.body:
I still play on PC, PlayStation, and Switch. I love Pokemon. Growing up has just given me more money to fund it. So I have a Formula 1-style simulator now.

Outside work, I'm an amateur guitarist and enjoy drones, golf, cooking, mixology, karting, sim racing, and dog whispering. I also blog, write poetry, and make lists. You may have noticed.
discoveries.summary: PC, PlayStation, Switch, Pokemon, and a Formula 1-style simulator. Also guitar, drones, golf, cooking, mixology, karting, dogs, blogging, poetry, and lists.

discoveries.heading: Memory and local AI
discoveries.body: I use OpenMemory and Qdrant for my agent's persistent memory. I also run speech, image, and voice services locally on Apple Silicon.
discoveries.summary: OpenMemory and Qdrant for persistent agent memory, with local speech, image, and voice services on Apple Silicon.
